The rigid family consists of linear combinations of basis functions $\{1, x, x^2\}$ with fixed coefficients (2D solution space), while the fat family consists of random linear combinations of $\{1, x, \dots, x^{10}\}$ with randomly sampled coefficients from a standard normal distribution, resulting in a high-dimensional solution space that cannot be captured by small networks.

The rigid family is defined by the conservation law $\frac{d}{dx}(f'(x)) = 0$ (implying $f'(x) = \text{constant}$, i.e., linear functions), while the fat family is defined by a stochastic transport equation with random diffusion coefficients, leading to a high-dimensional solution space that cannot be captured by small networks.
